review.decision_difference: Choose A to first establish whether Palamedes improves action-choice quality over strong and lightweight baselines; defer real-world outcome tracking until that controlled comparative advantage exists. B combines these stages, potentially turning an interpretable product-claim test into an inconclusive outcome experiment.
review.rationale: Both missions correctly frame comparative decision value as the binding uncertainty and reject feature expansion. A is more decision-improving because it isolates the full-system comparative effect with preregistered margins, budget and presentation controls, reviewer-stability checks, an explicit null policy, and a lightweight structured-prompt substitute. B prematurely requires downstream outcome attribution in the same pilot, introducing implementation, environmental, and measurement confounds that its own falsifiers acknowledge and making the smallest probe less bounded.

review.decision_difference: A tests whether the underlying bedtime-departure loop deserves priority before choosing voice; B commits product learning to the spoken version immediately. The key decision difference is demand-first sequencing versus simultaneous demand-and-voice validation.
review.rationale: A better improves the required sequencing decision by separating evidence of recurring departure demand from the cost, latency, and trust risks introduced by voice. It explicitly acknowledges the absence of behavioral evidence and uses a reversible text-only probe before committing to the spoken pipeline. B is highly specific and directly tests voice performance, but it pivots toward the more complex modality before establishing that self-departure itself is frequent and valuable. Both missions have bounded measurements and credible failure signals, though neither provides sharp numeric rejection thresholds.

review.decision_difference: A sequences a reversible controlled-agent experiment before choosing terminal, agent, hybrid, or stop; B chooses the agent-control pivot now and uses the experiment mainly to validate execution of that choice.
review.rationale: A best improves the required boundary decision because it acknowledges that the frozen evidence does not yet establish either user demand or lifecycle-protocol feasibility, preserves the evidenced terminal model, and defines a bounded comparative probe with explicit technical and user-value failure signals. B is highly specific and testable, but commits to the controlled-agent boundary before its own probe resolves the central uncertainties; its claim that existing foundations are better suited to agent supervision is plausible but not demonstrated by the supplied artifacts.
